title: The epidural was first described by a Spanish surgeon in 1921

scenes.text: The epidural, the anaesthesia we all associate with childbirth, was first described by a Spanish surgeon. And almost nobody knows his name.
Fidel Pagés, a military surgeon born in Huesca. In 1921 he publishes his technique in a Spanish journal: anatomy, method, cases and complications.
He called it metameric anaesthesia, because it numbs the body in bands. It's like switching off the lights on a single floor of a building, not on every floor below.
Two years later, Pagés dies in a road accident. He was 37.
In the 1930s, the Italian Dogliotti popularizes his own version without crediting him. Until an Argentinian surgeon, Alberto Gutiérrez, insists… and in 1939 Dogliotti acknowledges him.
Today the medical literature is clear: the epidural was first described by Fidel Pagés in 1921.
Share it with someone who has had one.
